sentences.show: In a Nazi castle prison, British officers secretly built a glider in the attic. Out of bed slats and sleeping bags.
Colditz Castle. A special prison for officers who had already escaped elsewhere.
On a cliff, above a river. Escape-proof, they said.
But one prisoner noticed the guards couldn't see the chapel roof. From there, you could fly over the river, 60 metres below.
In the prison library, they found a book on aircraft design.
Behind a fake wall in the attic, with lookouts and an alarm, they started to build.
Ribs from bed slats. Wing spars from floorboards. Control wires stolen from the castle's own cables.
The skin, blue and white prison sleeping bags, sealed with boiled millet porridge.
10 metres wide. And the launch? A bathtub full of concrete, dropped through the floor, to fling it off the roof.
By spring 1945 it was almost ready, a last resort in case the SS tried to massacre the prisoners.
Then the Americans arrived. The glider never flew. One photo was taken, and then it vanished.
55 years later, a replica flew, while the men who built the first one watched.
In 2012, a remote-controlled copy was launched from the same roof. It crossed the river, and landed safely.
So it would have worked. Would you have been the first to climb in?
They built wings to get out. One tap gets you in. Subscribe.
